name: FM electric-keys 'resonant tines' patch built on the subtractive analogy: modulation index as cutoff with its own envelope, a 10:1 bell ratio, a third operator with a no-sustain envelope, three macros (index, decay, ratio spread) and mod-wheel vibrato, aftertouch tremolo and an LFO auto-panner
goal: Design a playable FM keys/tines patch by treating FM depth (modulation index) like a filter cutoff. Start with two sine operators: slow modulator gives vibrato, then speed it up to audio rate to hear sidebands. A 1:1 ratio gives a saw-like full series; 2:1 shifts the spectrum (the presenter compares it to a square) and 10:1 gives the bell/tine. Shape the carrier with a multi-stage envelope (instant attack, short transient decay, sustain-like stage, release) and the modulator depth with its own envelope that starts rich and falls slightly. Add a third modulator operator with a fast-attack, no-sustain envelope, then build macros for index (brightness), decay (all falling-stage times) and modulator ratios (spread wide in opposite directions, a formant-like control). Finish with performance modulation (mod wheel → LFO vibrato from ~3.2 rate, aftertouch → VCA tremolo, a third controller → LFO panner) and a short delay plus bright light long reverb. More specific than generic FM bell skills: macro layout and expressive modulation for a keys patch.

source.title: Multiphonics CV-3 FM Core Patch Reconstruction with Adam—Resonant Tines
source.transcript_note: Sound-pack patch reconstruction; pack promo dropped and no pack content copied.

prerequisites: FM-capable synth or modular (operators with FM input, multi-stage envelopes); Web Audio: OscillatorNode modulators into a carrier's frequency AudioParam via GainNode index (implementation note)
Controller with mod wheel and aftertouch (or MPE)

inputs.name: carrier_ratio
inputs.description: Carrier frequency ratio (1 = in tune with the keyboard)

inputs.name: mod_ratios
inputs.description: Modulator ratios, e.g. 10:1 for the tine; also try 2 and 10

outputs.name: fm_keys_patch
outputs.description: Polyphonic FM resonant-tine keys patch with three macros

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Only the transcript's spoken values are used (8 Hz LFO-rate demo, ratios 1:1, 2:1, 10:1, LFO ~3.2). Envelope times are described shapes, not numbers.
Use carrier envelope to control level directly (no extra VCA needed when the operator has a level/envelope input).
Ratio-spread macro gives unpredictable results by design; cap ranges if it gets harsh.

steps.action: Patch one sine operator to the output with a spectrum analyser. Add a second operator at LFO rate (~8 Hz) into the first's FM input: you hear vibrato. Raise it to audio rate and key-track both from the keyboard to hear sidebands.

Compare ratios: 1:1 gives a saw-like spectrum with FM depth acting as cutoff; 2:1 changes the harmonic pattern (square-like per the presenter) and the harmonic tail detaches; 10:1 gives a classic FM keys/bell. Make the voice polyphonic.
steps.expect: Clear timbre changes with ratio; depth behaves like a filter

steps.action: Carrier amplitude: multi-stage envelope used like an ADSR (instant attack to max, short transient decay, a sustain-like third stage, last stage as release), gated by the keyboard.
Modulator depth: give the FM index its own envelope: rich at the start, falling slightly, staying fairly rich.

Add a third operator as an extra modulator with a fast attack and no sustain (falls to zero, a bit longer than the transient). Check the carrier stays at ratio 1 on the analyser while modulator ratios like 2 and 10 enrich the attack.
steps.expect: Spectacular evolving attack harmonics, pitch stays in tune

steps.action: Macros: (1) FM index across all modulators (brightness/'cutoff'), (2) decay: the falling-stage time of all envelopes, (3) modulator ratios moved wide in opposite directions (one up high, one down low) for a formant-like colour.

Performance mods: mod wheel speeds an LFO from ~3.2 and sets its level into all operators' fine-tune (slight detune for tremble/vibrato); aftertouch drives a biased VCA after the carrier for tremolo; a third controller drives an LFO panner. Add a short delay and a bright, light, long reverb.
steps.expect: Expressive tine keys with vibrato, tremolo and pan movement

verification: With index at zero only a sine is heard; raising the index adds harmonics, like opening a filter.
The fundamental stays at the played pitch for all modulator ratio settings.
Each macro audibly changes brightness, decay length or formant colour.
Mod wheel adds vibrato, aftertouch adds tremolo, and the panner moves the sound left to right.
